submission.natural_language_explanation: This pole fires on a token that completes a locally highly constraining one-to-two-token context: the current token has high transitional probability given the preceding word or two, e.g. fixed collocations ('upon' -> 'a'), verb-selected prepositions ('sat' -> 'on'), idiomatic subject-verb pairs ('recipe' -> 'calls'), keyword-selected identifiers ('SELECT' -> 'name'), and subword completions ('Se' -> 'ine'). It stays near baseline on the same common function words when the preceding context does not constrain them.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Yesterday I borrowed a bicycle from my neighbor and rode it downtown.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same peak token ' a' but after 'borrowed', which allows many continuations; hypothesis predicts no fire without a constraining predecessor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I left my keys on the kitchen counter this morning before work.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same peak token ' on' but after 'keys', which permits many prepositions; tests verb-selection claim since no selecting verb precedes it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: In my opinion, the movie is far too long and badly edited.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same peak token ' is' after 'movie', which takes many possible verbs; low transitional probability so hypothesis predicts baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: My neighbor's garden grows tomatoes, peppers, and fresh herbs.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same surface token ''s' as a possessive after 'neighbor' rather than the 'it is' contraction; preceding noun does not constrain it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The committee will name a winner tomorrow afternoon at noon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same token ' name' used as a verb after 'will', which can precede any verb; breaks the SELECT-keyword constraint.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He calls his mother every Sunday evening from Chicago.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same token ' calls' after the pronoun 'He', which predicts no specific verb; contrasts with the idiomatic 'recipe calls' driver.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I saw him in town yesterday morning near the station.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same token ' in' after the pronoun 'him', which allows many continuations; unlike the 'for i in' keyword context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She mentioned Friday only because the office closes early that day.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same token ' Friday' after 'mentioned', which does not constrain the next day-word; unlike the 'by Friday' deadline collocation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The times we shared together will stay in my memory forever.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same token ' times' after 'The', which can precede almost any noun; low transitional probability so predicts inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Upon further review, the committee rejected both proposals yesterday.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Contains 'Upon' but breaks the 'upon a' collocation with 'further'; tests that the driver alone without its completion does not fire the pole.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The cat wandered through the garden chasing butterflies all afternoon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same topic (cat plus spatial preposition) but no 'sat on' bigram; 'wandered' allows many continuations so predicts baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: He acted of his own accord without asking anyone for permission.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel fixed collocation 'own accord' where 'own' strongly constrains 'accord'; paraphrases the 'upon a' pattern in new words.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She apologized for breaking the antique vase during dinner.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel verb-selected preposition 'apologized for', where the verb strongly constrains 'for'; same mechanism as 'sat on' with new words.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: DELETE FROM archives WHERE year < 2000;
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel keyword-selected identifier in SQL, 'FROM archives', mirroring the SELECT-name mechanism in a fresh statement.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: His proposal ran into stiff opposition from the board last week.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel idiomatic verb-preposition pair 'ran into' where 'ran' strongly constrains 'into'; new context unlike the examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They spent Christmas in New York with old friends from college.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Novel high-transitional-probability proper noun 'New York', where 'New' strongly constrains 'York'; cross-genre holdout absent from examples.
